notes.note: Tested as runtime error: the actual sender (component type C) is stored in a variable of an incompatible component type D (D has an additional port).
NOTE 3 (CAN) tested as compile-time reject: integer value redirected to a boolean variable; this mismatch is statically detectable.

No from clause; the sender type (component type S) is determined at runtime and is incompatible with the sender variable type D, expected test case error. Close to test_032, which covers restriction c) itself.
'component' read as 'component type' (terminology). Violation: from clause AddressRef of type integer.
'component' read as 'component type' (terminology). Violation: sender clause ValueRef of type integer.

A port array that is not completely initialized cannot be written in TTCN-3 (component port arrays are always fully instantiated), so only the positive case is tested: any from on a complete port array, with the index checked.
Ambiguity: 'dimension' read as the number of dimensions (as in example 5: p[10][10] with v_i[2]). Violation: 3-element index array for a 2-dimensional port array.
'template in the from clause' read as the AddressRef in the from clause (terminology).
A signature template (not of a data type) is used as the trigger TemplateInstance. Restriction a) is unavoidably violated as well, because a message port cannot list a signature.
Ambiguity: reading 'the snapshot includes the port top element if present' chosen; the test checks that a queued reply is matched by the call body.
catch(timeout) cannot be written without a call timer, so the absence of a timeout exception is observed only indirectly: a reply delayed by 1 s is still handled by the call body.
Ambiguity: the descriptive reading was chosen (the reply is removed by getreply in a subsequent alt); the test also checks that the queue is empty afterwards.
Ambiguity: the obligation reading is not statically checkable; the test shows that exceptions are removed by catch in a subsequent interleave and that the queue is then empty.
Titan accepts this module: it does not check that inout parameters of a call have a specific value. The value list (1, 2) for an inout parameter violates restriction b).
Titan accepts this module: it does not reject AnyValue (?) for an in parameter in a call. This is prohibited explicitly by restriction b).
Connections are set up at runtime, so a missing to clause on a one-to-many connection is tested as a test case error (same convention as the 22.2.1 send test).
